title: Scheduled resilience rehearsals: Terraform IaC modules and health-check automation for Private VPC DR
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build an automated, repeatable workflow for running scheduled resilience rehearsals (DR drills) for Private (VPC) deployments across multiple regions. The work includes Terraform/IaC modules to provision ephemeral failover resources, orchestration scripts that run deterministic drills, automated health checks and smoke-tests post-failover, upgrade and rollback hooks for agent/runtime versions, and audit-ready logs for compliance.

Scope and deliverables:
- Terraform modules (infra-private-terraform/modules/drill) to create ephemeral DR staging stacks in a target region: routing entries, NAT/GW, peering/vpn stubs, minimal ingress, and a scaled-down inference pool for sanity checks. Modules must be param-driven (region, cidr, instance_profile, kms_key_id, rollout_strategy).
- Orchestration layer (Go-based CLI + GitHub Actions workflows) to trigger drills on schedule or ad-hoc. Support canary-run -> partial traffic shift -> full shift -> degrade -> rollback. Provide dry-run plan and enforced pre-check gates.
- Health-check automation: standardized probe suite (control-plane API ping, end-to-end generation with reference prompt set, KV-store consistency, prefix cache validation, metrics smoke tests) with pass/fail thresholds. Results written to centralized runbook dashboard and retained for 90 days.
- Upgrade/rollback hooks: ensure drills validate both platform and model rollout paths. Include automated rollback on quality regressions (regen-rate > threshold) or infra failures. Provide ABORT semantics and manual override with RBAC auditing.
- Observability and audit: drill run detail saved to S3 + structured events in our event bus. Dashboard panel (Console -> DR Rehearsals) with timeline, token counts, latency P95/P99, and error taxonomy.
- Runbook and SRE playbook: Confluence page + incident template + post-drill checklist.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Terraform modules modularized, documented, and published to the infra repo with tests.
2) A scheduled drill completes end-to-end in staging within 2 hours and records structured results.
3) Automated health checks detect injected failure (simulated region disk pressure or agent restart) and trigger rollback or alert within 5 minutes.
4) Drill artifacts (logs, metrics, PRs, runbooks) are linked from the ticket and retained per compliance policy.
5) Team run the first production-simulated rehearsal with a non-customer-impacting traffic shadowing strategy and sign-off from Security.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Ephemeral resources vs long-lived standby: Ephemeral stacks minimize cost but increase test complexity; we'll provision ephemeral stacks with a warm-builder snapshot to reduce boot time.
- Dry-run safety: All network mutations must be permission-gated. Dry-run differs from actual run: ensure dry-run never touches BGP/router configs in prod.
- Health-check determinism: Use a curated prompt set (stored in repo) to evaluate output stability. Tolerances configured per workload class (low-latency vs high-throughput).
- Cost controls: Add budget guardrails and automatic tear-down on timeout.

Run schedule proposal:
- Quarterly full rehearsal (multi-region, partial traffic shift)
- Monthly smoke rehearsal (ephemeral infra + health checks, no traffic shift)
- Weekly synthetic probes (health-check job only)
